question: What is the main purpose of a source water protection plan for a drinking water system?
correctAnswer: To identify and reduce risks to the raw water source before treatment
explanation: Source protection manages land use and activities around the source so contaminants are kept out of the raw water; treatment and sampling are still required.
options: To replace the need for filtration and disinfection at the plant
To set the price customers pay for treated water
To eliminate routine raw water sampling
To identify and reduce risks to the raw water source before treatment
sourceTitle: US EPA - Small Drinking Water Systems Handbook
sourceReference: Supporting resource category: Source Protection Awareness. See SOURCES.md: these are not claim-level verification citations.
optionA: To replace the need for filtration and disinfection at the plant
optionB: To set the price customers pay for treated water
optionC: To eliminate routine raw water sampling
optionD: To identify and reduce risks to the raw water source before treatment

question: Which activity near a wellhead most directly threatens groundwater quality?
correctAnswer: Storing fuel and chemicals without containment near the well
explanation: Uncontained fuel and chemicals can spill or leak into the ground and migrate toward the well, while routine site upkeep does not introduce contaminants.
options: Storing fuel and chemicals without containment near the well
Mowing the grass around the well casing
Posting a warning sign at the well site
Painting the pumphouse exterior on schedule
sourceTitle: US EPA - Small Drinking Water Systems Handbook
sourceReference: Supporting resource category: Source Protection Awareness. See SOURCES.md: these are not claim-level verification citations.
optionA: Storing fuel and chemicals without containment near the well
optionB: Mowing the grass around the well casing
optionC: Posting a warning sign at the well site
optionD: Painting the pumphouse exterior on schedule

question: What is a wellhead protection area?
correctAnswer: The land area around a well where activities are managed to protect the groundwater
explanation: A wellhead protection area is the surface and subsurface area around a well where land activities are controlled so contaminants cannot reach the groundwater supply.
options: The fenced yard inside the treatment plant
The land area around a well where activities are managed to protect the groundwater
The zone inside a reservoir where treated water is stored
The stretch of river downstream of an intake

optionD: The stretch of river downstream of an intake

correctAnswer: New activities can introduce contaminants that change raw water quality
explanation: Development, farming, and spills in the watershed can add contaminants to the source, so tracking changes gives the plant early warning of new risks.
options: Land use changes set the plant's chemical prices
Monitoring land use replaces the need for source sampling

Land use determines which licence class the operator needs

question: Which of the following is an example of a source protection measure at a surface water intake?
correctAnswer: Restricting fuel storage and waste disposal near the intake
explanation: Keeping fuel and waste away from the intake prevents contaminants from entering the source; the other choices are treatment adjustments, not source protection.
options: Restricting fuel storage and waste disposal near the intake
Increasing the filter backwash rate
Raising the chlorine dose for the whole year
Lowering the clear well operating level

question: Disinfection by-products form when chlorine reacts with which material in the water?
correctAnswer: Natural organic matter in the water

Natural organic matter in the water
Sand and anthracite filter media
Calcium hardness in the water

question: Which pair names the two groups of chlorination by-products most commonly monitored in drinking water?
correctAnswer: Trihalomethanes and haloacetic acids

Nitrates and phosphates

Trihalomethanes and haloacetic acids

question: Which raw water condition tends to increase disinfection by-product formation when chlorine is applied?
correctAnswer: High levels of natural organic matter in the raw water
explanation: More natural organic matter gives chlorine more material to react with, so by-product formation rises; alkalinity, turbidity, and oxygen do not have that effect.
options: High levels of natural organic matter in the raw water
Very low alkalinity in the raw water
A complete absence of turbidity
High dissolved oxygen in the raw water

question: What is the main operational reason plants remove organic matter before chlorination?
correctAnswer: Less organic matter means fewer by-products form during disinfection
explanation: Removing organic matter ahead of disinfection reduces the material available to form by-products, while a disinfectant residual is still required.
options: Organic matter makes chlorine gas too heavy to handle
Removing organics eliminates the need to maintain a residual
Less organic matter means fewer by-products form during disinfection
Organic matter raises the pressure in distribution mains

options: Chlorine only works when it is added to raw water
Applying chlorine after organic matter is removed reduces by-product formation
A later application point removes the need for contact time
The application point changes the chemical formula of chlorine

question: During a filter inspection, an operator finds mudballs cemented in the media bed. What is the most likely cause?
correctAnswer: Backwashing with too little energy or too short a duration to clean the bed

Filtering at a rate well below the design rate
Using anthracite media above the sand layer
Sampling the filter effluent too often

Add coagulant directly onto the filter bed
Lower the clear well level to pull more flow through
Run the filter to waste until the effluent turbidity clears before returning it to service

question: An operator suspects air binding in a gravity filter, shown by bubbles in the bed and a loss of driving head. What condition most often causes air binding?
correctAnswer: Dissolved air coming out of solution as pressure falls through the bed
explanation: As water passes through the bed and pressure drops, dissolved air can come out of solution and collect in the media, blocking flow and causing air binding.
options: Backwash troughs installed above the media
Dissolved air coming out of solution as pressure falls through the bed
Media grains that are too uniform in size
Effluent valves that open too slowly

The cracks will seal themselves within one filter run
Cracking increases the effective size of the media
A channelled bed gives lower head loss and better quality water

explanation: Dissolved iron and manganese pass through filters, so they are first oxidized into solid particles that the filter can then strain out.
options: Oxidation makes both metals dissolve more completely
Oxidation converts the dissolved metals into particles that filtration can remove
Filtration removes the metals only while they stay dissolved
Oxidation turns both metals into harmless gases

It boils the hardness out during regeneration
It swaps calcium and magnesium ions for sodium ions held on the resin
It precipitates hardness using chlorine
